summary: An Indologist who studied under Citrapati (~1795–1801), Colebrooke served in the Bengal Civil Service, taught at Fort William College (1782–1814), and served on the Supreme Council of Bengal (1807) and the Council of India (~1807–1812).

An expert in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics, Tolman studied at Yale University (~1884–1890). He taught at Wisconsin (1891–1892), North Carolina (1892–1894), and Vanderbilt University (1894–1923).
An Indologist and historian-archaeologist, Risley was educated at Winchester College (~1863–1869) and New College (~1869–1873).

Working in Indology and archaeology, Härtel studied under Ernst Waldschmidt at Göttingen (~1948–1953). He served as director at the Museum für Asiatische Kunst Berlin (1963–1986) and held professorships at Humboldt University and Freie Universität Berlin.
A scholar in Indology and philosophy, Randle served as professor of philosophy at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1910–1927) and later as Librarian at the India Office Library (1927–1949).

A Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology scholar, Guenther studied at Munich and Vienna under Wilhelm Geiger and Wilhelm Havers. He held posts at Lucknow (1950–1958), Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1958–1963), and Saskatchewan (1964–1984).

A linguist who studied at Swarthmore, Harvard, Leipzig, and under Hermann Sauppe at Göttingen (1881–1884), Smyth held faculty appointments at Bryn Mawr College (1887–1901) and Harvard University as Eliot Professor of Greek Literature from 1901.
A Japanologist who studied under Karl Florenz (~1928–1932), Zachert held academic posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1936–1941) and the University of Bonn (~1960–1977).
A scholar of Indology and linguistics, Kellgren studied under Hermann Brockhaus, Eugène Burnouf, and Philippe-Édouard Foucaux. He held a post at the University of Helsinki (~1849–1856).

A specialist in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, Beckh studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1902–1907) and Kiel University. He later held posts at Humboldt University (~1908–1921) and the Prussian State Library (~1912–1921).
An Indologist and linguist, Berger completed doctoral and habilitation studies under Helmut Hoffmann (~1950–1955). He later held a post at Heidelberg University (~1964–1995).
A scholar in Indology and linguistics, Beythan was educated by traditional teachers Ramasami Aiyar and Radscha Pillai.

A philosopher who studied at the universities of Leipzig and Berlin, Bonitz held posts at the University of Vienna (~1849–1867) and the Prussian Ministry of Spiritual, Educational and Medical Affairs (~1867–1888).

An Indologist and linguist, Brockhaus studied under August Wilhelm von Schlegel at Bonn. He served as professor at the University of Jena (1839) and long-term professor and Rektor at the University of Leipzig (~1841–1877).

An Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber and earned a PhD at Zurich, Brunnhofer worked as a translator at Saint Petersburg State University (1891–1901) and as a Dozent at the University of Bern (1901–1914).
An Indologist, Kellner studied under Hermann Brockhaus and subsequently served as a Gymnasialprofessor at Gymnasium Zwickau.

A linguist and Indologist, Collitz studied under August Fick at Göttingen and at Halle. He held academic posts as Dozent at Bryn Mawr College (1885–1907) and professor of Germanic Philology at Johns Hopkins University (1907–1928).
After studying at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1876–1880), Grassmann served as a professor at the University of Giessen (~1904–1922).

An Indologist and art historian, Goetz studied at Munich and under Jean Philippe Vogel. He was curator at Baroda Museum (1939–1953), director of the National Gallery of Modern Art (1953), and director at Heidelberg University (1961–1976).

Grassmann worked in linguistics, Indology, and other fields, studying under Friedrich Schleiermacher in Berlin (1827–1830). He taught at several institutions in Stettin, including as professor at the Marienstiftsgymnasium (~1852–1877).
